thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1976543210 created — KV-cache surge + continuous-batching regression causing batch-scheduler starvation in multi-tenant pools. Paging oncall @maya_oncall :rotating_light:

maya_oncall: saw alerts for high tail latency and dropped headroom on 4/5 GPU pools. Customer reports increased 95th/99th for generation endpoints. Investigating now.

santiago_runtime: noting a large uptick in KV cache size + frequent invalidations around 11:12 UTC. Seems correlated with the new prefetch tweak we rolled earlier today.

alex_sre: can you paste the spike graph? which metric exactly?

maya_oncall: attaching quick snapshot —

```
/metrics/gpu_pool/latency_95: +320ms
/metrics/kv/cache_size_bytes: +2.3GB
/metrics/batch_scheduler/queue_time_p99: 1.9s
```

maya_oncall: impact: several production customers on hosted tier saw generation 95/99 spikes, some requests timed out and retried. We have automated mitigation suggestion queued.

incident-bot: @oncall handoff suggested -> escalate to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Ops runbook: try batching-window shrink + disable aggressive prefetch for affected pools.

santiago_runtime: hypothesis: prefetch introduced extra KV churn causing eviction storms -> hot-key thrash -> continuous batching queues up long requests that hold KV handles, starving short requests.

samir_platform: confirm. We're seeing mixed long/short request interference in the mixed-workload pools (multi-tenant). Short tails are getting queued behind multi-token long gens.

alex_sre: mitigation plan (fast): 1) set batch_scheduler.max_pack_time=20ms (was 80ms) 2) toggle kv.prefetch.enabled=false for pools p-3,p-4 3) enable pack fairness by token-size.

maya_oncall: executing step 1 now.

ops-bot: Command: kubectl -n inference set env config/batch-scheduler max_pack_time=20ms --record
ops-bot: 4 pods rolling restart initiated.

maya_oncall: rolling restarts go green. Observability shows queue_time_p99 dropping from 1.9s -> 420ms within 45s. latency_95 down ~140ms.

santiago_runtime: I'm patching a targeted change to disable prefetch on the affected pools:
```
# quick hotfix
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/configs/pools/p-3 -d '{"kv": {"prefetch": false}}'
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/configs/pools/p-4 -d '{"kv": {"prefetch": false}}'
```

samir_platform: applied. cache churn reduced; eviction rate back to baseline.

emily_cs: Customer status: CS has flagged 3 enterprise accounts that reported retries/timeouts. Reached out; they saw ~30-40s of elevated errors, then gradual recovery. No data exfiltration.

alex_sre: good. Can we run a quick canary for fairness tweak? Add policy: pack_preference=short-first for packs >8 requests.

santiago_runtime: deploying canary to p-5 (10% traffic) now.

ops-bot: canary applied; telemetry shows improvements on p-5 immediate — short request latency p95 down 60%.

maya_oncall: monitoring for regressions. Also toggled alert thresholds to avoid noisy pages while we stabilize.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1976543210 update: mitigation steps applied (batch_pack_time reduced, prefetch disabled on affected pools, short-first pack policy canary). Customer impact: partial for hosted customers on mixed pools; no major data loss; services recovering.

santiago_runtime: root cause (prelim): recent prefetch optimization introduced background reads that increased KV caching churn under mixed workloads. Combined with a batching config tuned for throughput (high pack_time) this allowed long-running pack owners to block short requests — scheduler fairness not robust to KV eviction pressure.

alex_sre: action items (immediate):
- revert prefetch auto-aggressive behavior behind a gate for mixed pools (owner: santiago_runtime)
- bake a fair-packing scheduler policy (short-first by default) (owner: alex_sre)
- add eviction-pressure alarms and KV churn dashboards (owner: samir_platform)
- postmortem and customer impact notes (owner: emily_cs)

emily_cs: leaving note: customers A, B, C impacted. CS has notified account teams and offered post-incident call.

maya_oncall: timeline for postmortem? I'd like a write-up and diff of the prefetch change.

santiago_runtime: I'll pull the PR/link: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/pull/4829 — change was "prefetch: more aggressive heuristics for long-context models". Reverting to previous heuristic as part of hotfix.

ops-bot: Hotfix commit pushed: 9f3b2d7 — revert aggressive prefetch heur. Deploying to affected pools with gradual rollout.

maya_oncall: final check: latency normalized across pools, eviction rates stable, queue_time_p99 < 500ms for all.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1976543210 resolved -> monitoring for 2 hours; schedule postmortem and follow-ups.

alex_sre: postmortem notes will include: timeline, contributing factors, config knobs we tuned, and proposed automated guardrails (auto-disable prefetch under eviction-spike and pack_time adaptive lowering).

emily_cs: customer comms draft: "We experienced degraded token latency and elevated timeouts for a subset of hosted generation workloads due to an aggressive runtime prefetch optimization interacting with batching behavior. Mitigations applied and service stabilized. We'll follow up with root cause and corrective actions."

maya_oncall: closing: leaving handoff to next oncall. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
